issues.description: Extract the layer-statement check into a named predicate instead of an inline negated compound.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag the new guard `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` as hard to read. Pull it into a named local like `const isLayerStatement = nodeName === 'layer' && !node.nodes` so the rule expresses intent forward rather than as a double-negative reaching into AST shape.

issues.description: Replace `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` with `!node.nodes` to match codebase idiom.
issues.detail: PostCSS distinguishes container from leaf at-rules by presence of a `nodes` array. The `typeof === 'undefined'` form is ceremony that couples this rule to an AST implementation detail; `!node.nodes` (or a `hasBlock` helper) states the same fact more crisply and matches surrounding style.

issues.description: Add a paired accept-case test for statement-form `@layer foo;` (and anonymous `@layer {}`) before `@import`.
issues.detail: The added fixture covers only the block-form reject case. A complementary accept test for `@layer foo, bar; @import ...` pins the new semantics so a future refactor cannot quietly re-merge the two layer forms. Torvalds also suggests covering anonymous `@layer {}` to round out the regression net.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously agrees the fix is small, scoped, and correct: a block-form `@layer foo {}` should block following `@import` while statement-form `@layer foo;` should not, and the diff distinguishes them by `node.nodes` presence. All three reviewers raise the same readability concerns — the inline double-negative predicate should be named, and `typeof === 'undefined'` should become `!node.nodes` to match codebase idiom. Test coverage should be rounded out with a paired accept case for statement-form layers. No correctness blockers; ship after a small readability and test pass.
